text: Thanks — I can reproduce it: in middleware/proxy.go both balancers index into the target slice without checking for an empty list (randomBalancer.Next calls rand.Intn(0), roundRobinBalancer.Next does % 0). A subagent is fixing both to return nil on an empty target list (and making sure the proxy middleware itself doesn't dereference a nil target), while verifying the existing test suite stays green. ETA ~6 minutes.

Got it. That's in echo.go's ServeHTTP / Context.SetPath: on the no-route-matched path the requested URL is stored as the context path, so c.Path() can't distinguish "no route" from a real match. A subagent is on it (it will also check no existing test depends on the old behavior), verifying with a real server that matched routes still report their route path. ETA ~8 minutes. The balancer panic fix from your first report is done and being independently verified now.

Fixed and independently verified. In middleware/proxy.go both balancers now return nil when the target list is empty (randomBalancer.Next guards len(targets)==0 before rand.Intn; roundRobinBalancer.Next guards before the modulo, and now takes the balancer's mutex so the empty check and index update are consistent). The proxy middleware also handles a nil target instead of dereferencing it: it returns 503 Service Unavailable. Verified with a throwaway program (outside the repo): NewRandomBalancer(nil).Next(c) and NewRoundRobinBalancer([]*ProxyTarget{}).Next(c) both return nil with no panic, also after removing the last target and under concurrent churn; a normal proxy request still returns 200 from upstream. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` clean, `go test ./... -count=1` and `go test -race ./...` all pass — no pre-existing test touched or broken.

Understood. Context.Scheme() currently trusts whatever X-Forwarded-Proto / X-Url-Scheme contains without validating it, so a bogus value like "ftp" wins over the valid fallback. A subagent is fixing it to accept only valid schemes, fall back to the next header, and finally default to http (https when TLS), keeping the existing precedence. It will verify with a throwaway program and the full test suite. ETA ~8 minutes.

Got it. In bind.go the map-binding path assigns the raw string value into the map's element type, so a map[string][]string element gets a string (hence the reflect panic) and map[string]interface{} only ever gets the first value. A subagent is fixing it so repeated keys collect all values ({"tag": ["a","b"]}) without panicking, while keeping struct/slice binding and any existing test expectations intact. ETA ~9 minutes.

Confirmed the shape of it: Group's route registration mangles the path when the group prefix is combined with an empty route path (the first group ends up registered under a different path than the one you request), so the second group's registration makes /group unreachable. A subagent is fixing the path normalization in group.go/echo.go so GET /group hits g1's handler with m1 and GET /group/other hits g2's with m2, without touching any existing test. ETA ~9 minutes.

Fixed. In context.go, Scheme() now validates each header value before accepting it: only "http"/"https" (case-insensitive) are accepted from X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Protocol and X-Url-Scheme; anything else falls through to the next source, ending with the http/https default (https when the request is TLS). So X-Forwarded-Proto=ftp + X-Url-Scheme=https now gives "https", and ftp alone gives "http". The precedence order and TLS behavior are unchanged, and the valid set matches the Context interface doc ("http or https"). Verified with a throwaway program (12 cases incl. your repro) and `go test ./... -count=1` — all green, no existing test modified.

Right — with the gzip middleware the writer wrapper emits a gzip stream for an empty body but the Content-Encoding header never gets set, so the client sees binary garbage. A subagent is fixing compress.go so the body and the Content-Encoding header always agree (empty body either uncompressed or a valid gzip stream with the header), keeping non-empty compression and the other compressors intact. ETA ~9 minutes.

Fixed. In router.go, Router.Find used to pre-seed the context path with the *requested* URL and only overwrite it on a successful match; it now clears the path and sets it only to the registered route path once a route matched. So c.Path() is "" for unmatched requests (404) and still the registered route path for matches, e.g. "/users/:id" for GET /users/42. Verified with a real server: 200 -> "/users/:id", "/static/*" for wildcards, 404 -> "", and no existing test depends on the old behavior (checked by reverting the fix in a copy: suite still green). `go test ./... -count=1` and `go test -race ./...` pass, no test file touched.

Status: the balancer panic (#1), c.Path() on unmatched routes (#2) and Scheme() validation (#3) are fixed and verified. Still in progress, each with its own agent running the full test suite plus a throwaway repro program: map binding with repeated keys (#4), same-prefix groups (#5), and the empty-body gzip header mismatch (#6). Estimates: #4 ~3 min, #5 ~3 min, #6 ~4 min.
